docs.title: AppSec Discovery
docs.text:
AppSec Discovery turns code into an inventory of the objects that carry data: database tables, API routes, gRPC methods, GraphQL operations, DTOs, Terraform resources. Every object has fields; rules mark the objects and fields that hold sensitive data (PII, payment, authentication secrets, ...):

  • keyword rules match names (last_name, card_number, a combination of fields),
  • LLM rules ask a model (any OpenAI-compatible API) with a prompt you write.

Every rule match is a hit with a status: pending_review, match, no_match or need_more_info. In the service, LLM verdicts go through a tiered review: the service model categorises everything, a harness model (a capable model in an agent harness connected over MCP) checks what the service model was unsure about and a sample of what it was sure about, and a human decides the rest in the UI.

There are two ways to use it:

CLI / Python package appsec-discovery Service (appsec_discovery_service/) Input one source folder GitLab projects, polled over the API (main branches and open MRs) Rules conf.yaml edited in the UI / REST / MCP, stored in Postgres Output YAML / JSON / SARIF report inventory, hits and decisions in Postgres; UI, REST API, MCP server LLM optional, one endpoint the service model + optional harness model + human review

docs.text:

Project

  • Changelog
  • Contributing

• Closed MRs with a deleted source branch (service, scanner): a scan_mr whose source branch is gone because the MR was merged / closed (or deleted) in GitLab meanwhile ends as skipped instead of failing; a deleted source of a still open MR, or a state GitLab cannot tell, fails as before.
  • Disk guards of clones (service, scanner): no clone starts while the workspace has less than WORKSPACE_MIN_FREE_GB (5) free (a retried failure with the cause on Pipeline health); SCAN_MAX_REPO_MB (0 = off) refuses repositories GitLab reports larger (permanent); MR sources that need their history are partial clones (--filter=blob:none, GIT_PARTIAL_CLONE); a clone that fills the disk reports no space left on device and its partial checkout is removed at once; compose mounts the workspace as the volume scan_workspace (SCAN_WORKSPACE_VOLUME: a host directory on another disk).
  • UI at scale (service, discovery_ui): the Review page opens on a cluster board (the open hits grouped by same schema / same field / same object name / rule x group, GET /hits/clusters) with Decide cluster (POST /hits/decide: dry run, "Apply to N" with expected_total, a toast with Undo and a "Recent decisions by filter" section) and "Decide all" on any filter in the list view; the flat list with keyboard triage stays as a view and inside a cluster; the Questions tab stays one by one. The tabs, the menu badge, the Work desk tiles, the Pipeline "Human" tile and the Group view count the same queues from one GET /hits/aggregate (the Work desk tiles showed wrong captions and three different numbers for one queue). Lists show estimated totals ("about N rows", an exact count on click) and page by keyset cursor. Statistics come from the snapshots with ETag and "updated N s ago"; polling waits for the previous answer, slows down in hidden tabs and backs off on errors. A scope bar (GitLab group, kept in the URL) narrows every list and count; a project page (/projects/:id/show) and a Group view (/groups) replace the project searches; Jobs filter by project. Server-side autocompletes (/rules?q=, /categories, /object_types, /groups?q=) replace the 500-rule and overview dropdowns. Hit rows, the verdict card and object rows carry In main / Only in open MR / Gone chips. Pipeline health shows the real typical run / wait times and ETAs, the escalation overflow, the worker pools and limits, collapses idle kinds and says the reach of its actions ("Parse first 200 of N"). Service tokens can be created with scope mcp (the connect snippet shown once); the Harness snippets take a token placeholder. Every API cap is said on the page ("N of M shown", "top 200"). See UI.
  • API and MCP at scale (service, migration 0032_scale_api): hit presence filters read the stored in_main / in_open_mr flags (manual labels refresh them); list totals are estimates above 10 000 rows (X-Total-Estimate, exact=true for a count) and lists page by keyset cursor (after / X-Next-Cursor) next to range; GET /objects lists the main snapshot without a DISTINCT ON over every live row and computes the per-row figures for the page only; GET /overview, GET /jobs/health, GET /scan_progress / GET /llm_progress totals and GET /llm_quality are served from the scanner's statistics snapshots with computed_at, ETag and 304; GET /jobs/health typical_run_s / typical_wait_s / eta_s are no longer null (jobs.started_at). Review at scale: GET /hits/aggregate (counts by queue / rule / category / project / group ... in one call), GET /hits/clusters (schema / field pattern / object name / rule x group clusters of the open hits), POST /hits/decide (one decision on every hit of a filter: dry run, expected_total, human decisions kept, review_batches, POST /hits/decide/{id}/undo, batch_id in the verdict history); the cluster and group filters of GET /hits. Autocompletes: GET /rules?q=, GET /categories, GET /object_types, GET /groups; group=<prefix> on hits / objects / projects; GET /projects/{id} is the project page (hits by rule, objects by type, open MRs, jobs; GET /jobs?filter={"project_id"}). MCP: response byte cap (MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES, truncated + hint), cursor paging and estimated totals, summary views of get_hit / get_object, scan_progress without the project list by default (include_projects=true or a filter), per-client service tokens with scope mcp (POST /tokens; reviewer and lease owner token:<name>, accepted on REST too) and a per-client rate limit (MCP_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE), ui_url deep links (UI_BASE_URL), new tools hits_aggregate, hits_clusters, decide_hits, undo_decision, review_batches, list_groups, get_project. Prompt trial samples use TABLESAMPLE. See REST API, MCP server, Tiered review.
  • Pipeline at scale (service, migration 0031_scale_pipeline): the GitLab sync gets a worker pool of its own (SYNC_WORKERS, 2) and the control jobs theirs (CONTROL_WORKERS, 1), so harness verify items, external answers and rollouts never wait behind thousands of project syncs; a sync reads only the default branch and the MR branches by name, the MR states in one batched call, and skips projects without new GitLab activity (SYNC_UNCHANGED_EVERY_H, 24; polling only, no webhooks). LLM throughput: LLM_CONCURRENCY (2) model calls in flight per LLM worker, verdicts stored in chunk order; LLM_RATE_PER_MIN (0 = off), a token bucket in Postgres shared by every worker and replica. Harness escalations capped at LLM_ESCALATION_DAILY_MAX (2000) per rule and UTC day, the overflow counted (escalation_overflow in the verify job, job_health.escalations). Relabel / adopt of a rule version's verdicts as an llm_relabel job in slices (lifecycle.enqueue_relabel, batch_jobs=True) instead of one UPDATE in the API transaction. stats_refresh job (STATS_REFRESH_S, 60) writes the stats_snapshots (overview, job_health, scan_progress, llm_progress, llm_quality, hits_aggregate; shared SQL in discovery_common/stats.py) the API serves while fresh. jobs.started_at stays on finished rows, so GET /jobs/health typical_run_s / typical_wait_s / ETA are no longer null; expired leases are reaped by the scheduler, not on every claim. The compose file forwards every scanner setting (GITLAB_CACHE_TTL_S, GIT_TIMEOUT_S, JOB_POLL_S, LLM_ROLLOUT_QA_*, ...) and rotates the logs of every container (LOG_MAX_SIZE 50m x LOG_MAX_FILE 5). See Jobs and workers, Scanning, Tiered review, Configuration.
  • Storage at scale (service, migration 0030_scale_storage): hit presence stored on the row (rule_hits.in_main / in_open_mr, maintained by the scanner on every snapshot, MR and branch change, backfilled) with partial indexes for the live list, the open queue and the retention; stored LLM hashes (object_fields.llm_hash, objects.names_hash) so candidate selection and coverage no longer hash every field per run; coverage groups only by what a rule's patterns look at; indexes rule_hits (object_key), rule_hits (project_id, rule_id), objects (name, object_key), jobs ready-by-kind; rule_hits fillfactor 85 and autovacuum settings; the snapshot diff of a main scan is linear in the branch size (was quadratic: minutes for a 300k-object branch); orphan GC in one pass; retention of harness verifications (LLM_VERIFICATIONS_RETENTION_DAYS, 365) and finished prompt trials (PROMPT_TRIALS_RETENTION_DAYS, 90); stats_snapshots for precomputed statistics; Postgres memory / planner settings in the compose file (PG_*). See Data model, Retention, Configuration.
  • Diff-based scan skip (service): a new main branch commit or MR activity that changes no file a parser reads moves the snapshot without a clone, a parse or an LLM run (GitLab compare API; SCAN_DIFF_* settings; migration 0029_diff_skip; GET /jobs/health scans). Full MR scans take the changed files from the compare API and clone the source shallow. Core 1.1.0: Parser.file_patterns, appsec_discovery.affected_parsers. See Scanning.
  • Failure causes in the UI: jobs.last_error carries the real cause of a failed scan or LLM run (the git fatal: line, the parser that broke, the per-rule summary of an LLM run; discovery_scanner/services/failures.py), credentials stripped (discovery_common/redact.py); GET /jobs/errors groups failures by cause, GET /llm_rules/{id}/errors collects a rule's failed objects, runs and refused harness answers. Permanent causes (a deleted MR branch, a configuration error) fail at once without retries.
  • LLM rules lifecycle (LLM rule lifecycle): rule versions (rule_versions; the Versions tab with diff, cost estimate, activate, rollback), budgeted rule rollouts of the stale verdicts (llm_rollouts, the llm_rollout controller job, pause / resume / cancel, auto-pause on a harness agreement drop), explicit stale-while-revalidate (stale / stale_reason on hits, filter stale, answered_stale in the LLM coverage), the verdict history of every LLM hit (hit_verdicts, GET /hits/{id}/history, the hit page tab History), core prompts versioned per family (classifier3 / rule3) and pinned per rule version, the service model tracked per version, jobs.priority. Behaviour change: a prompt / scope edit, an accepted proposal, new core prompts or another LLM_API_MODEL no longer re-ask every machine verdict in the next runs: the verdicts stay (flagged stale, still scoring) and a rollout - started by a human (LLM_ROLLOUT_DEFAULT=canary)
  • asks them again within LLM_ROLLOUT_CALLS_PER_HOUR; accepting a prompt proposal makes a candidate version. The previous behaviour: LLM_REASK_INLINE=true, LLM_ROLLOUT_DEFAULT=immediate, LLM_CORE_BUMP_MODE=immediate, LLM_MODEL_CHANGE_POLICY=ignore. Migrations 0024_rule_versions, 0025_hit_verdicts, 0026_llm_rollouts. New MCP read tools llm_rule_versions, llm_rule_version_estimate, llm_rollouts, llm_rollout, hit_history.
  • Stored object names are renamed (migration 0027_object_names): stored versions get the new names without the type prefix and the LLM hits' names_hash is recomputed, so the rename asks nothing again. Rules whose patterns still contain an old type word (^Route, Struct dto, Table, Rpc, Mutation, Query, Virtual machine...) are not rewritten: the migration lists them in its log - drop the word and use object_type_re. Run this revision online (the rename is computed in Python).
  • Built-in rules (migration 0028_builtin_rules): the keyword scoring rules are renamed kw-fields / kw-props and are disabled on a new install (existing installs keep their state); disabled, no score_tags hit is recorded. The env-managed LLM rule is removed: LLM_PROMPT / LLM_PROMPT_VER are gone (ignored when still set), the rule synced from them is soft-deleted (or only disabled when it has human decisions); create a classifier rule (an LLM field rule without category) in the UI if you used it. A second default LLM rule api-with-auth (disabled) is seeded on new installs.
  • Object names no longer contain the object type (it is object_type): graphql Mutation X.f -> X.f, protobuf Rpc /pkg.Svc/Method -> /pkg.Svc/Method, swagger Route /path (GET) -> GET /path, python routes Flask route /path calls Get handler (GET) -> GET /path (get), python / golang / java Pydantic dto User / Struct dto User / Jpa entity User -> User, javascript JS GQL Resolver me in query GetUser -> GetUser.me, migrations Table public.users -> public.users, terraform Resource aws_s3_bucket.logs / Module x -> aws_s3_bucket.logs / x, Virtual machine vm -> vm. Object identities (hash, the service object_key) are unchanged. Breaking for config patterns that include the type word: object of score_rules, object_name of exclude_scan / exclude_scoring (^Route /admin, Struct dto, ...) no longer match; drop the word and add object_type (and parser): {object_type: route, object: 'POST /admin'}. Names may now repeat across types; nothing keys on the name. SARIF messages keep the [<parser>.<object_type>] prefix.
  • Hit statuses renamed to the verdict words: confirmed -> match, rejected -> no_match (pending_review and need_more_info stay). Who decided is decided_tier (service | harness | human). The reviewer actions keep their names (confirm / reject / request_info / reopen). Migration 0023_match_statuses rewrites rule_hits.status, machine_status, the status suffix of verify_key, llm_verifications.service_status, trial items and open verify items. For one release the REST / MCP status filters and the library's apply_hit_statuses / RuleHit(status=...) accept confirmed / rejected as aliases; every output has the new values only. The aggregate keys human_confirmed / human_rejected (dry run) and confirmed_by_category (overview) and the settings HITS_DECIDED_UNSEEN_DAYS / HITS_REJECTED_UNSEEN_DAYS keep their names. Roll out the API, scanner and UI together with the migration.
  • Tier names (migration 0021_service_tier): the tiers are service (was weak) and harness (was strong) - rule_hits.decided_tier, llm_verifications columns service_status / service_verdict / service_model, the verify items' context keys; the API / MCP / UI say "service model" and "harness model". The hits filter decided_tier still accepts weak / strong for one release; the GET /llm_quality keys (service_verdicts, service_unsure, harness_decisions) and llm_mislabeled items (harness_verdict) are renamed without aliases. VERIFY_PROMPT_VERSION 2. The UI role "Engineer" is now "Datasec".
  • Alerting removed, read-only GitLab. The service no longer posts MR comments or Telegram messages and never writes to GitLab: a token with read_api + read_repository is enough. The settings MR_ALERTS, TG_ALERT_TOKEN, TG_CHAT_ID and ALERT_TIMEOUT_S are gone (ignored), get_mr has no alert_candidates, MRs and hits no alerted_at / alerted. Migration 0022_no_alerts turns keyword rules with action: alert into score rules. The REST / MCP rule API accepts action score | exclude only. action: alert in conf.yaml is deprecated: accepted for one release as score with a warning.
  • Default rules of a new service installation: migration 0013_example_rules seeds the LLM object rules db-tables-with-client-data (enabled) and api-with-auth (disabled), mode auto.
  • Default mode auto for new rules: LLM rules default to mode auto like keyword rules (was review); auto hits are a match at once but stay in the harness QA sample. MCP create_rule / update_rule use the same defaults as the UI / REST (allow_auto is accepted and ignored).
  • UI: the "Merge requests" page is removed (MR data stays available through GET /mrs, GET /mrs/{id}, POST /mrs/{id}/scan and the MCP tools list_mrs / get_mr / scan_mr); the keyword rule action "Alert" is gone.
  • Graceful shutdown of the scanner on SIGTERM: running jobs are requeued at their next safe point, a service LLM run keeps the verdicts it already got (SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S).
  • CLI: the in-process llama.cpp backend (ai_local, llama-cpp-python) was removed; every model is reached through the OpenAI-compatible ai_api client. An ai_local section still loads as a deprecated alias.

docs.title: Objects, hits and scoring
docs.text: The data model is the same in the CLI report and in the service database.

docs.title: Objects and fields
docs.text:
A CodeObject is one thing a parser found: an API route, a gRPC method, a GraphQL operation, a DTO / entity class, a database table, a Terraform block.

key meaning hash identity of the object: parser, type, name and position-independent content (the service's object_key is built from it); lines are never part of it object_name the name without a type word: GET /user/login, /pkg.Svc/Method, Queries.promoterInfo, public.users, User object_type route, rpc, query, mutation, subscription, dto, entity, table, resource, data, module, variable, output, provider, ... parser the parser that produced it file, line where it is properties name / value pairs such as path and method of a route fields the fields (field_name, field_type, file, line, comment, samples), named by their path: query.param.username, input.SumInput.n1, output.Payload.firstName comment documentation taken from the code (cut at 1000 characters) severity, tags the score: computed from the match hits hits every rule match on the object or its fields

Field samples (at most 5 of 200 characters) are values seen in the code: defaults, enum values, examples. Secrets never become samples: samples of secret-named fields (password, token, api_key, client_secret, dsn, ...) and secret-looking values (PEM keys, user:pass@ URLs, Bearer / Basic credentials, JWTs, cloud / VCS tokens, long random strings) are dropped by every parser.

docs.title: Hits
docs.text:
A hit is one match of one rule on one subject: a field, a property or the object itself (subject: field | prop | object). It carries the rule (rule, rule_type keyword / llm, rule_id, rule_version), the matched keyword (keyword rules) or the model's reason and model (LLM rules), the fields that made an object match (combination rules, object LLM rules), severity, tags and a status:

status meaning pending_review the rule runs in mode review (or the hit was reopened): waits for a decision, does not score match the rule applies: scores the subject (mode auto hits are a match at once) no_match the rule does not apply: listed, never scores (LLM rules store negative verdicts so a subject is not asked again) need_more_info the model was unsure, or a reviewer asked for more information: waits, does not score

Reviewer actions keep their verbs: confirm -> match, reject -> no_match, request info -> need_more_info, reopen -> pending_review. Transitions: pending_review -> need_more_info | match | no_match; need_more_info -> match | no_match | pending_review; match / no_match -> pending_review. The old statuses confirmed / rejected are accepted as aliases by the library (apply_hit_statuses, RuleHit(status=...), with a deprecation warning) and by the service's status filters for one release; every output has the new names only.

In the service a hit also records who decided (decided_tier: service | harness | human, see Tiered review) and, for human decisions, the reviewer and decided_via (rest | mcp).

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Only match hits score. A field's severity is the highest severity of its match hits and its tags are their tags (pii, auth, llm-pci, ...). An object's severity is the highest of its own and its fields' hits; its tags are the union, plus the tags of the rules whose hits matched (personal-data, gdpr). Objects without a match have no severity. appsec_discovery.apply_hit_statuses(objects, {hit.key(obj.hash): status}) applies stored decisions and recomputes everything.

Severities: critical > high > medium > low > info.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• YAML / JSON: the objects as above, hits under hits.
  • SARIF 2.1.0: a result per scored object ([<parser>.<object_type>] <name>) and per scored field (...: field <name>), the hits in properties.hits; a result whose hits all wait for a decision has kind: review and level: none.

docs.title: CLI and Python package
docs.text: The appsec-discovery package scans one source folder and prints the objects it found, scored by the rules of a conf.yaml. It runs the parsers (most of them on the Semgrep OSS engine with bundled rules, some on their own scanners) and, optionally, LLM rules against any OpenAI-compatible API. Models never run inside the process, so pip install needs no native build.

docs.title: Install and run
docs.text:
pip install appsec-discovery
appsec-discovery --source path/to/project                 # default keyword rules, YAML to stdout
appsec-discovery --source path/to/project --config conf.yaml --output report.json --output-type json

Options (appsec-discovery --help):

option meaning --source DIR the folder to scan (required) --config FILE conf.yaml, see Configuration; without it the default score_tags keywords apply --output FILE write the report to a file instead of stdout --output-type yaml|json|sarif report format (default yaml) --only-scored-objects report only objects with a severity / tags --fail-on-error exit 1 when any parser failed (by default only when every parser failed) --fail-on-severity low|medium|high|critical exit 1 when an object of this severity or higher was reported (CI gate) -v / -vv log level INFO / DEBUG (default WARNING)

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 every parser failed, any parser failed with --fail-on-error, or the severity gate fired; 2 invalid arguments or config.

Example output (swagger sample, keyword rules):

- hash: 40140abef3b5f45d447d16e7180cc231
  object_name: GET /user/login
  object_type: route
  parser: swagger
  severity: high
  tags: [auth]
  file: swagger.yaml
  line: 1
  properties:
    path: {prop_name: path, prop_value: /user/login, severity: medium, tags: [auth]}
    method: {prop_name: method, prop_value: GET}
  fields:
    query.param.username:
      field_name: query.param.username
      field_type: string
      severity: medium
      tags: [auth]
    query.param.password:
      field_name: query.param.password
      field_type: string
      severity: high
      tags: [auth]
  hits:
    - rule: kw-fields
      subject: field
      field_name: query.param.password
      keyword: password
      severity: high
      tags: [auth]
      status: match

What the fields of an object mean, how hits turn into severity and tags, and the statuses a hit can have are described in Objects, hits and scoring. The objects each parser produces are in Parsers.

docs.title: Reports and CI/CD
docs.text:
--output-type sarif writes SARIF 2.1.0 that vulnerability management systems import (DefectDojo: "SARIF" scan type). Each object is one result with its hits in properties.hits; hits that wait for a decision (pending_review / need_more_info) are results of kind: review.

appsec-discovery --source . --config conf.yaml --output report.sarif --output-type sarif --fail-on-severity high

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
import appsec_discovery

result = appsec_discovery.scan("path/to/project", "conf.yaml")           # a path, a dict or a ScoreConfig
result = appsec_discovery.scan("path/to/project", {"score_tags": {...}}, project="grp/payments-api")
objects, failed = result.objects, result.errors                            # {parser name: error message}
report = appsec_discovery.render_report(objects, "sarif")

# apply decisions stored elsewhere (the service does this) and recompute the scores
appsec_discovery.apply_hit_statuses(objects, {hit.key(obj.hash): "match"})

scan(source, config=None, *, ai=None, only_scored=False, project=None, llm_backend=None) returns a ScanResult (objects, errors, parsers); parser failures do not raise. project scopes the rules with a project / projects glob; llm_backend runs the LLM rules on an injected LlmBackend (tests, the service's external executor). load_config, load_config_file, run_parsers, ScanPipeline, AiScorer, REPORT_FORMATS are exported too. appsec_discovery.affected_parsers(changed_paths, parser_names) and parser_file_patterns() (core 1.1.0) tell which parsers a set of changed files can affect (Parser.file_patterns); the service's diff-based scan skip uses them.

Errors: ConfigError (bad config), UnknownParserError, SemgrepError, all subclasses of AppsecDiscoveryError; the CLI maps them to the exit codes above.

docs.title: Configuration: conf.yaml
docs.text:
appsec-discovery --config conf.yaml. Every section is optional; without a config file the default score_tags keywords apply and no LLM runs. The schema is appsec_discovery.models.ScoreConfig.

parsers: [all]            # or a list: swagger, protobuf, graphql, javascript, migrations, terraform, java, golang, python
object_types: [all]       # or: route, rpc, query, mutation, subscription, dto, entity, table, resource, ...
score_tags: {...}         # keyword rules on field / property names (below)
score_tags_mode: auto     # auto (default) | review
score_rules: [...]        # keyword rules limited to particular objects (below)
llm_rules: [...]          # LLM rules, see "LLM scoring in the CLI"
ai_api: {...}             # the LLM endpoint every LLM rule runs on
exclude_scan: [...]       # drop objects before scoring
exclude_scoring: [...]    # suppress particular keyword hits

docs.title: score_tags: keywords by category and severity
docs.text:
A keyword matches a field name or a property value (a route path) as a case-insensitive substring (or as a regex from the start). A hit gives the field / property its severity and the category as a tag; the object gets the highest severity and the tags of its hits.

score_tags:
  pii:
    high: [first_name, last_name, phone, passport]
    medium: [address, email]
    low: [city]
  finance:
    high: [pan, card_number]
    medium: [amount, balance]
  auth:
    high: [password, pincode, codeword, token]
    medium: [login]
score_tags_mode: auto     # auto: hits are a match at once; review: hits are pending_review and do not score yet

The built-in default (appsec_discovery/models/config.py):

category high medium low pii full_name, fullname, first_name, firstname, last_name, lastname, phone, passport, ssn address, email city finance pan, card_number, cardnumber account_number, accountnumber, balance, amount - auth password, pincode, codeword, token login, email, phone, username -

Severities: critical, high, medium, low, info. An unknown severity key is a config error.

docs.title: score_rules: keyword rules on particular objects
docs.text:
Matchers are Patterns: a regex matched from the start of the value, or a case-insensitive substring; parser is an exact name. A rule with field_name / field_type hits fields, otherwise the object. object and field are accepted as short aliases of object_name and field_name.

score_rules:
  - name: cards-in-dtos
    object_type: dto
    field_name: card
    severity: critical
    tag: pci
    mode: auto                   # auto | review (hits wait for triage and do not score until a match)
  - name: admin-routes
    object_name: /admin          # the name has no type word: "POST /admin", not "Route /admin"
    object_type: route
    tag: admin
    action: score                # score (default) | exclude
    project: payments/*          # optional project glob (library API: scan(..., project=...))
  - object_name: Legacy
    action: exclude              # suppresses every hit on Legacy* objects, like exclude_scoring
  - name: person-contact         # a combination of fields: one hit on the object
    fields_all:                  # groups: regex searched in the field name, case-insensitive
      - last_?name|surname|full_?name
      - phone|msisdn
    min_groups: 2                # optional: how many groups must match (default: all)
    fields_none: [masked]        # optional: no field may match
    tag: pii
    severity: high
    tags: [personal-data]        # object tags added once the hit is a match

A fields_all rule hits the object, not single fields, and the hit lists the fields that matched (fields): a last name with a phone is a hit, a first name with a phone is not. One decision covers the whole combination.

tags (any score_rules / llm_rules entry): once a hit of the rule is a match, these tags are added to the object; its fields keep the hit's own tag.

action: alert is deprecated: still accepted for one release, treated as score with a warning.

docs.title: Exclusions
docs.text:
exclude_scan:                    # objects dropped before scoring; all set criteria must match
  - parser: swagger
    file: generated/
  - object_type: dto
    object_name: ^Internal
exclude_scoring:                 # keyword hits suppressed (LLM hits are not affected)
  - field_name: password_hash    # criteria: file, parser, object_name, object_type, prop_name, field_name, field_type, tag, keyword
    tag: auth
  - keyword: token               # the score_tags keyword that hit, exact
    object_name: TokenType

prop_name criteria only apply to hits on properties, field_name / field_type only to hits on fields; a rule with no criteria never matches.

docs.title: Patterns and the object name
docs.text: Object names carry no type word (it is object_type): GET /user/login, /pkg.Svc/Method, public.users, User, GetUser.me, aws_s3_bucket.logs. Patterns on the name match the rest (/admin, ^GET); use object_type (and parser) for the kind. See Parsers for the names each parser produces.

docs.title: LLM scoring in the CLI
docs.text: Keyword rules only know names. An LLM rule asks a model about the object and its fields, so it finds sensitive data without a keyword list. The CLI talks to every model through one OpenAI-compatible client (the ai_api section); models never run inside the CLI process.

docs.title: 1. An endpoint
docs.text:
Local model - the official llama.cpp server with any GGUF model from Hugging Face serves an OpenAI-compatible API on http://localhost:8080/v1:

docker run -d --name llm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -v llm_cache:/root/.cache \
  ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-b12098 -hf Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# or: docker compose -f docs/local-llm.compose.yml up -d     (LLM_HF_REPO / LLM_MODEL_FILE / LLM_MODELS_DIR)

The first start downloads the model into the llm_cache volume; later starts work offline. A GGUF file you already have: -v /path/to/models:/models -m /models/<file>.gguf. Small instruct models (3B, Q4) are fast on common hardware and good enough for this classification task; try other models and prompts.

External API - any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works the same way (base_url, api_key, model).

ai_api:
  base_url: "http://localhost:8080/v1"   # or https://api.deepseek.com, ...
  model: "local-model"                   # llama.cpp serves its one model under any name
  # api_key: "..."                       # not needed for a local server
  # system_prompt: "You are a data security bot ..."   # the built-in classifier's prompt
  # timeout: 120                         # seconds per request
  # max_retries: 2                       # connection errors, 429 and 5xx are retried
  # max_tokens: 8192
  # structured: auto                     # auto | json_schema | json_object | none (response_format)

appsec-discovery --source tests/swagger_samples --config tests/config_samples/ai_conf_local_server.yaml

docs.title: 2. The built-in classifier
docs.text:
An ai_api section alone runs one implicit rule (llm-default): the classifier. Each object is one request: the model gets the object name and its candidate fields (ids, dates, paging fields are skipped) and answers with JSON {"fields": [{"name": ..., "category": "pii|finance|auth|other"}]}, enforced with response_format where the server supports it. Every flagged field gets severity medium and an llm-<category> tag; an object whose request fails is reported without LLM tags.

- object_name: GET /user/login
  object_type: route
  severity: medium
  tags: [llm-pii, llm-auth]
  fields:
    Input.password:
      severity: medium
      tags: [llm-auth]

docs.title: 3. llm_rules
docs.text:
llm_rules replaces the classifier with any number of rules that all run on the ai_api endpoint (llm_rules: [] disables LLM scoring):

llm_rules:
  - name: pci-fields
    category: pci                # hit tag llm-pci (or set tag)
    severity: high
    system_prompt: You look for payment card data (PAN, CVV, expiry) in API fields.
    prompt_version: 1            # bump on every prompt change; stored with each hit
    target: field                # field: the model picks matching candidate fields; object: judges the whole object
    mode: review                 # auto (default) | review
    object_types: [route, dto]   # optional scope: object_types, parsers, projects (globs)
  - name: person
    category: pii
    target: object
    mark_fields: true            # object rules only: the fields the model names get hits too
    tags: [personal-data]        # object tags once the hit is a match
  • Field rules (target: field) get the object and its candidate fields and name the matching fields: one hit per field. A field rule without category and tag is the classifier with your system_prompt.
  • Object rules (target: object) get the whole object (type, file, properties, every field with its type, comments and samples) and judge it: one hit, with the fields that make it match in fields. An object rule needs a category (or tag). The prompt can describe combinations ("match only when the object identifies a person: a last name together with a phone, document or birth date; a first name alone is not enough").
  • mark_fields: true (object rules): the same single call also gives one field hit per named field, with the rule's status, tag, severity, reason and version. Field hits are ordinary field hits and are decided independently of the object hit.
  • The model answers match, no_match or need_more_info; need_more_info hits never score and wait for triage.

The code-derived text (names, comments, samples) is sent inside a delimited <object> block that the prompts declare as untrusted data, never as instructions. The core prompts are versioned (PROMPT_VERSION of the classifier, RULE_PROMPT_VERSION of the rules, both 3); every hit stores the rule's prompt_version and the model.

docs.title: Migrating from ai_local
docs.text: The in-process llama.cpp backend (llama-cpp-python) was removed. An ai_local section is a deprecated alias of ai_api with base_url: http://localhost:8080/v1 (override with ai_local.base_url) and model: <model_id>; model_folder and gguf_file are ignored with a warning. Serve the same model with a llama.cpp server (-hf <model_id>, or -m with your GGUF file) and switch the section to ai_api when convenient.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
The core package is managed with uv (Python 3.12, pyproject.toml, uv.lock); .devcontainer/ has a ready container.

uv sync --locked                        # the package, its dependencies and the dev group (pytest, alembic, sqlmodel, psycopg2)
uv run appsec-discovery --source tests/swagger_samples
uv run pytest                           # core tests; the Postgres-backed ones need TEST_DATABASE_URL

Service tests run in their own environments against a real Postgres (TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...):

cd appsec_discovery_service
uv run --no-project --with-requirements discovery_api/requirements-dev.txt pytest discovery_api/tests
uv run --no-project --with-requirements discovery_api/requirements-dev.txt pytest discovery_common/tests collectors/tests

.github/workflows/python-package.yml runs the same: core + scanner + discovery_common tests, the API / MCP tests, image builds of the API, UI and scanner, the nginx config check, a docs link check, and the package build (published to PyPI on a release).

docs.title: Writing a parser
docs.text:
A parser is a class in appsec_discovery/parsers/<name>/parser.py that registers itself by its name (appsec_discovery/parsers/base_parser.py, REGISTRY; add the module name to BUILTIN_PARSERS in parser_factory.py):

  • SemgrepParser - ships scanner_rules/*.yaml next to the module; each rule declares metadata: {parser, object_type, framework} and its findings are dispatched to handlers[object_type], which build CodeObjects from the metavariables. Declare file_patterns (the languages' files, e.g. ('*.go',)).
  • FileParser - walks the source tree (vendored directories pruned, files read with read_text_file: symlinks out of the tree, special files and files over 5 MB skipped), parses every file matching globs (which become file_patterns) and builds the objects.

Rules of the road: object identity is object_identity(parser, relative file, object_type, logical_name) - lines are never part of it; object names carry no type word (it is object_type); fields are named by their path (input.Message.field, output.*, query.param.x); comments go through clean_comment (cut at 1000 characters), samples through the secret filter (never a password / token / key value); every parser must survive an untrusted repository (no network, no following symlinks, bounded memory).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• tests/<name>_samples/ holds the inputs of a parser, tests/fixtures/<parser>/semgrep.json the recorded Semgrep results (the golden tests need no Semgrep binary) and tests/golden/<parser>.parsed.json / .scored.json the expected objects (test_golden.py, golden_support.py); regenerate them after an intended change of a parser's output and review the diff.
  • tests/test_file_parser_safety.py and tests/test_ai_prompt_injection.py are the safety suites every parser and prompt builder must pass.
  • The service: discovery_scanner/tests, discovery_api/tests, discovery_common/tests (migrations are tested against a real Postgres, including the query plans of the candidate queries).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: docs/ is a mkdocs-material site (mkdocs.yml, extra docs dependency group: uv sync --group docs && uv run mkdocs serve). The README stays short and links into docs/; CI checks that every link resolves. No internal project names, hosts or secrets in examples (grp/payments-api).

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text: Fork, branch, run the tests, open a PR against main with a changelog line in docs/changelog.md for anything a user can notice (a setting, an endpoint, a migration, a behaviour change).

docs.title: Parsers
docs.text:
parsers: [all] (the default; PARSERS=all in the service) runs every parser below except the deprecated ones. Parsers based on Semgrep run the engine with the bundled scanner_rules/*.yaml; the others have their own file scanners. Files are read only inside the scanned folder (symlinks pointing out of it, FIFOs and devices are skipped), up to 5 MB (Terraform and specs 10 MB); non-UTF-8 files are decoded with replacement.

parser reads (file_patterns) objects swagger *.yaml / *.yml / *.json: OpenAPI 3.x and Swagger 2.0 (2.0, e.g. protoc-gen-openapiv2 / grpc-gateway output, is converted to 3.0); a file counts when its top-level key is openapi / swagger and it has paths route <METHOD> <path> per operation: <in>.param.<name>, input.* (request body, 2.0 body / formData), output.* (the first response defining a field); recursive schemas are cut at the self reference, remote $ref are not fetched, a broken spec / operation is skipped with a warning protobuf *.proto rpc /<package>.<Service>/<Method>: request / response messages with nested messages, oneofs and maps (at most 2000 fields per request / response) graphql *.graphql / *.gql schemas (graphql-core) query / mutation / subscription <Type>.<field>: an operation of a root type (the roots declared in schema { ... }, else Query / Mutation / Subscription; a business type Subscription used as a field type is an entity): args by name (id, card.number), result type up to 5 levels as output.*; fields of extend type are operations. The files of a directory are one schema, a directory joins its parent's schema unless both define a type of the same name (two services of a monorepo are two schemas) javascript gql tagged templates in *.js / *.jsx / *.ts / *.tsx / *.mjs / *.cjs (graphql-core) query / mutation / subscription <Operation>.<field>: a resolver call of a client operation: arguments (typed from the operation variables) as input.*, the requested selection with fragments (from any file) as output.* migrations *.sql: PostgreSQL migrations - goose / sql-migrate (Up part), golang-migrate *.up.sql, numbered .sql files table <schema>.<table> of the final schema of a migrations directory (statements replayed in version order: CREATE / ALTER / DROP / RENAME, partitions folded into their parent), one field per column terraform *.tf, *.tf.json (own HCL scanner; .terraform/ skipped) resource, data, module, variable, output, provider blocks named by their address (aws_s3_bucket.logs, x): attributes as fields (nested blocks as block.attr), the value kind as the type (string / number / bool / list / map / reference / expression); modules with vm_* attributes are the vm objects of earlier versions. Secret attributes (password / token / key..., sensitive = true, PEM / token-like values) never become samples: they are listed in the sensitive_fields property java *.java (own source scanner + the Semgrep @Table / @Column rule; test sources, build/, target/, generated dirs skipped) dto <Class> (@Table(name) classes), entity <Outer.Inner> (JPA @Entity / @Table / @MappedSuperclass / @Embeddable, javax / jakarta / spring-data / hibernate, JDBI @ColumnName: fields named by their column), dto <Outer.Inner> (records, Lombok @Data / @Value / @Builder, Jackson, Gson, @Schema classes: Java field names). Add entity to object_types filters that list types golang *.go (Semgrep; files up to 5 MB, generated *.pb.go included) dto <Name>: struct fields of basic types (type X struct, grouped type ( ... ), generic structs, A, B T; fields of anonymous nested structs as Outer.Inner.Field) python *.py / *.pyi (Semgrep) dto: pydantic / dataclass (@dataclass(...) too) / sqlalchemy / django / mongo / marshmallow models (fields with defaults included); route <METHOD> <path> (<handler>): fastapi / flask / django / bottle / starlette routes client, db nothing deprecated: find nothing, not part of all, accepted in an explicit list with a warning for one release

migrations: each migrations directory is its own schema. ClickHouse DDL, test(s) / testdata / fixtures / seeds / datafixes directories are skipped, and next to migration histories so are schema dumps (structure.sql). DDL built at run time (EXECUTE '...' in DO blocks) and the columns of CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT are not known.

The file_patterns are also what the service's diff-based scan skip compares the changed files of a commit against (appsec_discovery.affected_parsers).

docs.title: Comments and samples
docs.text:
Objects get a comment and fields a comment and samples taken from the code (omitted when the code has none; a comment is cut at 1000 characters, at most 5 samples of 200 characters):

parser comment samples protobuf // / /* */ above the rpc / field or at the end of its line values of enum fields graphql descriptions ("...") and # comments defaults, values of enum types javascript the JS comment above the gql template, # comments in it literal arguments, variable defaults migrations -- above CREATE TABLE / a column or after it, COMMENT ON DEFAULT, CHECK (col IN (...)) swagger summary / description, property / parameter description example(s), x-example, enum, default golang, java, python, terraform comments / javadoc / docstrings above the struct, class, field, route, module example / enums / default tags, @Schema(example), allowableValues, pydantic Field(example=...) and literal defaults

Secrets never become samples, whatever the parser (see Objects, hits and scoring). Comments and samples are shown next to the fields in the LLM prompts, in the UI and over MCP (get_object, list_objects(comment=...)), and are accepted by POST /ingest (send masked or synthetic samples).

docs.text:
openapi: 3.0.3
paths:
  /user/login:
    get:
      summary: Logs user into the system
      parameters:
        - name: username
          in: query
          schema: {type: string}
        - name: password
          in: query
          description: The password for login in clear text
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        '200':
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {type: string}

appsec-discovery --source tests/swagger_samples

- object_name: GET /user/login
  object_type: route
  parser: swagger
  severity: high
  tags: [auth]
  file: swagger.yaml
  comment: Logs user into the system
  properties:
    path: {prop_name: path, prop_value: /user/login, severity: medium, tags: [auth]}
    method: {prop_name: method, prop_value: GET}
  fields:
    query.param.username: {field_name: query.param.username, field_type: string, severity: medium, tags: [auth]}
    query.param.password: {field_name: query.param.password, field_type: string, severity: high, tags: [auth],
                           comment: The password for login in clear text}

docs.title: Service: overview and quick start
docs.text: The service (appsec_discovery_service/) keeps the inventory of a GitLab instance up to date: it polls the GitLab API for projects under configured prefixes, clones main branches and open merge requests, parses them with the core package, applies the rules edited in the UI and stores objects, hits and decisions in Postgres. People and agents review the hits in the UI, over the REST API and over MCP.

docs.title: Components (docker-compose.yml)
docs.text:
container what it does discovery_scanner the scanner: a supervisor with a scheduler (GitLab polling, periodic jobs) and worker processes that run the jobs of the Postgres queue - MAX_WORKERS scan workers, SYNC_WORKERS GitLab sync workers, CONTROL_WORKERS control workers, LLM_WORKERS LLM workers (service model runs, LLM_CONCURRENCY calls in flight each). Built from the repository root so it uses the core package sources (pinned appsec-discovery>=1.1.0,<2.0.0) discovery_llm the bundled llama.cpp server (OpenAI-compatible API at http://discovery_llm:8080/v1), the default service model; downloads LLM_HF_REPO into the llm_cache volume on first start; scaled to 0 when an external API is used discovery_migrate one-shot Alembic migration (python -m discovery_common.migrate); the API and the scanner start after it succeeded discovery_api FastAPI: REST under /api (OpenAPI UI at /api/docs) and the MCP server at /api/mcp; the same bearer token for both discovery_ui the React (react-admin) UI discovery_db Postgres 13, data in $HOME/db_data discovery_nginx the only published port (HTTP_PORT, default 80): the UI at /, the API at /api/, login rate limit on /api/token (5 per minute per client)

Networks: edge (nginx, UI, API), backend (internal, no route outside: Postgres, migrate, API, scanner, LLM), egress (the scanner for GitLab, the LLM for the model download). Postgres, the API and the LLM server are not reachable from the host; docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up publishes Postgres on 127.0.0.1:54321 (POSTGRES_DEV_PORT) for local debugging or a BI tool.

GitLab API ──poll──> scanner ──clone / parse / rules──> Postgres <── API (REST + MCP) <── nginx <── UI, agents, scripts
                        │                                  ▲
                        └── service model (discovery_llm or any OpenAI-compatible API)
                                       harness model (an agent harness over MCP) ─┘

The service only reads GitLab (project / branch / MR lists, MR state, clones over HTTP) and never writes to it: no MR comments, notes, labels, statuses, no webhooks. Objects added or changed in an MR are stored as the MR's delta and reviewed like the rest (presence "Only in open MRs"); MR data is available through the API / MCP (list_mrs, get_mr, scan_mr), there is no MR page in the UI.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Requirements: Docker Compose v2.20+ with BuildKit (the default since Docker 23; the compose file uses depends_on.required and per-Dockerfile .dockerignore), a GitLab token with the scopes read_api and read_repository (a project / group access token or a personal token of a user with the Reporter role).

git clone https://github.com/dmarushkin/appsec-discovery
cd appsec-discovery/appsec_discovery_service
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env - the required part:

POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<random>
GITLAB_URL=https://gitlab.example.com
GITLAB_PRIVATE_TOKEN=<read-only token>
# comma separated, matched on path segments: "grp/" = every project of the group, "grp/proj" = that project
# only (not grp/proj-tools); a trailing * keeps a plain string prefix ("grp/proj*")
GITLAB_PROJECTS_PREFIX=grp/
GITLAB_SCAN_TYPES=mains,mrs
UI_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com
# bcrypt hash in single quotes (a plain UI_ADMIN_PASSWORD and well-known passwords are refused at startup):
#   python -c "from passlib.context import CryptContext; print(CryptContext(schemes=['bcrypt']).hash('<password>'))"
UI_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH='$2b$12$...'
# at least 32 random characters: openssl rand -hex 32
UI_JWT_KEY=<random>

docker compose up --build                       # with the bundled local model
docker compose up --build --scale discovery_llm=0   # with LLM_API_URL / LLM_API_KEY / LLM_API_MODEL set to an external API

Open http://127.0.0.1/ and log in with UI_ADMIN_EMAIL and the password. The scanner syncs the projects of the prefixes, scans their main branches and open MRs and runs the enabled LLM rules; see Scanning for what happens when and Configuration for every setting (LLM_API_URL= empty disables LLM rules).

First things to do in the UI: check Pipeline health (Admin role) while the first scans run, then switch to Datasec and look at the Review queue and the default rules (db-tables-with-client-data is enabled, api-with-auth is disabled) under LLM rules - see Rules and UI.

To connect an agent (a harness model) use the MCP server at http://127.0.0.1/api/mcp with a bearer token from POST /api/token - see MCP and Tiered review.

docs.title: Production notes
docs.text:
• Put a TLS terminator in front of nginx and declare it in discovery_nginx/conf.d/real_ip.conf (copy real_ip.conf.example, set its address / CIDR): otherwise every request comes from the terminator's address and the login rate limit of /api/token is shared by all clients.
  • Bake the images in your own registry / Kubernetes and use an external Postgres (DATABASE_URL is what the services read; the compose file builds it from POSTGRES_*).
  • Upgrade the migrate, API, scanner and UI images together: the migrations change constraints that older versions cannot write (discovery_migrate runs before the API and the scanner start).
  • For analytics connect Superset, Grafana, Tableau, ... to Postgres (see the dev compose override for publishing it).
  • Postgres settings: the compose file starts the bundled Postgres with shared_buffers 1 GB, work_mem 32 MB, effective_cache_size 3 GB, random_page_cost 1.1, max_wal_size 2 GB (PG_* variables, see Configuration) - sized for an 8 GB host shared with the scanner and the LLM server. An external Postgres needs the equivalent; with the image defaults the planner falls back to sequential scans at millions of rows.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: Behind nginx at /api (uvicorn --root-path /api); the interactive OpenAPI UI is at /api/docs. Every call except /health needs Authorization: Bearer <token> from POST /api/token (username + password form fields; rate limited to 5 per minute per client by nginx) or a service token with scope mcp (POST /tokens; identity token:<name>, refused by the admin-only token endpoints). Lists follow the react-admin simple-rest conventions: ?range=[0,24]&sort=["id","ASC"]&filter={"status":"pending_review"}, the page size is capped, the response carries Content-Range. Service errors map to 400 / 403 / 404 / 409 / 413 / 422 / 429.

docs.title: Paging at scale
docs.text:
GET /hits, GET /objects and GET /projects (millions of rows):

  • the total of Content-Range is exact up to 10 000 filtered rows and an estimate above (the planner's row estimate; header X-Total-Estimate: true). exact=true (query parameter, or "exact": true inside filter) forces an exact count;
  • keyset paging: every page answers X-Next-Cursor (absent on the last page); after=<cursor> (query parameter, or "after" inside filter) returns the rows after the previous page in the same sort order at the cost of one index probe, whatever the depth. A cursor is bound to the sort it was made with (422 otherwise). range (offset) keeps working for react-admin; after resets the offset to 0. GET /projects sorted by pending_hits (a count computed per row) answers no cursor: offset paging only;
  • group=<path> on these three lists scopes to a GitLab group (a prefix of full_path: grp/payments matches grp/payments/ledger, not grp/payments-old); GET /groups lists the groups.

docs.title: Statistics snapshots
docs.text:
GET /overview (without arguments), GET /jobs/health, GET /scan_progress / GET /llm_progress (totals), GET /llm_quality (without rule_id) and GET /hits/aggregate are served from stats_snapshots, recomputed by the scanner's stats_refresh job every STATS_REFRESH_S (60 s) and served while younger than twice that. The answer carries computed_at and snapshot (true from the table, false computed live - filters, a stale or missing row, live=true). Snapshot answers get a weak ETag and Cache-Control: max-age until the next refresh; a request with If-None-Match gets 304 Not Modified - poll freely.
