What agents cannot do over MCP: accept a prompt proposal, activate a rule version, start / pause a rollout, create service tokens - these are for humans in the UI or REST.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
The cleanup job (control worker, every GC_INTERVAL_HOURS, default 24; 0 disables it; guarded by an advisory lock so only one process collects) deletes in batches of GC_BATCH_SIZE (5000):

what when setting (default) closed / merged MR rows closed_at older than MR_ROW_RETENTION_DAYS (7) the tracked source branch of an open MR without activity (and its delta) not updated for MR_STALE_DAYS (30) untracked branches, orphan object versions (no branch has them; collected in one anti-join pass, deleted by key in batches) at once - scan markers of a branch beyond the newest N SCANS_KEEP_PER_BRANCH (20) pending_review hits whose subject is in no branch (in_main and in_open_mr false, see presence) older than HITS_PENDING_ORPHAN_DAYS (14) match / need_more_info hits in no branch last seen older than HITS_DECIDED_UNSEEN_DAYS (180) no_match hits in no branch last seen older than HITS_REJECTED_UNSEEN_DAYS (365; the name predates the status rename) finished jobs (done / failed) older than JOBS_RETENTION_DAYS (7); the newest job of every kind is kept for the scheduler external work / verify items: open ones expire, finished ones are deleted older than 7 days (llm_work.RETENTION_DAYS) verdict history rows (hit_verdicts) older than; the last row of every version of a subject is kept HIT_HISTORY_DAYS (180) harness verifications (llm_verifications; the QA metrics read the last 30 days) older than; 0 keeps them LLM_VERIFICATIONS_RETENTION_DAYS (365) finished prompt trials with their items (a trial a proposal refers to is kept) older than; 0 keeps them PROMPT_TRIALS_RETENTION_DAYS (90) ingest upload sessions left open after 24 hours

Decisions on objects that disappear from the code are therefore kept for the retention above and come back with the object when it reappears (same object_key). The hit retention reads the partial index hits_seen (COALESCE(last_seen_at, first_seen_at), status; hits in no branch only), so a batch costs milliseconds whatever the table size. The cleanup logs table statistics afterwards (GET /health/db).

docs.title: Rules and hits in the service
docs.text:
Rules live in the rules table and are edited in the UI (Keyword rules, LLM rules), over REST (/api/keyword_rules, /api/llm_rules) and over MCP (create_rule, update_rule, get_rule, list_rules, delete_rule). Rule edits apply on the next scan of each project; keyword rule edits make the branches rescan once by themselves, LLM rule runs are started by hand or after scans. Hits and their statuses are described in Objects, hits and scoring.

Every rule has name, category, severity (critical .. info), mode, enabled, tags (object tags once a hit is a match) and a scope: project_re, parser (exact), object_re, object_type_re, field_re, field_type_re - patterns matched from the start of the value (regex) or as a case-insensitive substring.

Modes: auto - hits are a match at once (and stay in the harness model's QA sample); review - every hit waits in the review queue as pending_review. New rules default to auto and enabled, in the UI, REST and MCP alike; pass mode: review / enabled: false to stage one. An update without mode keeps the rule's mode.

Deleting a rule is a soft delete (deleted_at, enabled = false): hits keep their rule.

docs.title: Keyword rules (kind = keyword)
docs.text:
Besides the scope: action (score | exclude - exclude rules suppress every hit on the matching subjects and produce none) and field combinations fields_all (groups of regexes searched in the field names, at most 20), fields_none, min_groups. A rule with field_re / field_type_re / fields_all hits fields (a combination: the object, listing the fields), otherwise the object. They are mapped to the core's score_rules and evaluated by the scan itself.

Built-in keyword rules (scope.source = core, migration 0028_builtin_rules): kw-fields (the score_tags keywords in field names) and kw-props (in the object's properties) - disabled on a new install; enable them, switch their mode or set tags in the UI (nothing else of them is editable). Disabled, the core records no score_tags hit.

POST /rules/dry_run (MCP dry_run_rule): what a keyword rule would hit on the stored main snapshots, with how many of those subjects people already set to match / no_match, without writing anything; for an LLM rule the number of model calls a run would make. GET /rules/stats (MCP rule_stats): per rule and version, the precision of human decisions and the top reject notes.

docs.title: LLM rules (kind = llm)
docs.text:
Besides the scope: target (field | object), prompt (the system prompt, up to 20000 characters), mark_fields (object rules: the fields the model names get hits too). An LLM field rule without category is the built-in classifier (pii / finance / auth / other). How field and object rules work, what the model sees and mark_fields are described in LLM scoring in the CLI; the service adds versions, re-asks and rollouts (LLM rule lifecycle) and the tiered review (Tiered review).

LLM rules run with the service model (LLM_API_URL, LLM_API_MODEL):

  • after every successful main scan (every enabled rule) and MR scan (on the delta), when LLM_API_URL is set;
  • on demand: POST /llm_rules/run (MCP run_score_rules, UI "Run" on the LLM rules page): {"rule_ids": [6, 7], "project_ids": [1, 5], "mrs": false} over the stored snapshots (no clone, no parse). Only subjects without a current verdict are sent, so a second run costs nothing. "executor": "external" (UI: "Harness model (answers via MCP)") runs the rule with a model outside the service: External executor.

Verdicts: a positive answer is a match (mode auto) or pending_review (mode review), need_more_info is a machine need_more_info hit in the review queue, a negative answer is a machine no_match hit so the subject is not asked again. Every LLM hit stores the model, the model's reason, the rule version and the core prompt version it was made with.

Coverage: GET /llm_progress (MCP llm_progress; Pipeline health "LLM coverage", the Projects page's "LLM rules" column) says how far the LLM rules got: per main branch exactly one of current (every enabled rule has a fresh row with nothing remaining), failed (the last llm_score / llm_prepare job of the branch failed), never (a rule not counted yet), outdated (subjects remain or a row is stale), not_scanned; queued / running / awaiting_answers; per rule answered / total / remaining, answered_stale, pending_external, failed, projects_current; the same for open MRs; projects with the same filters as /scan_progress (?status=failed,never, incomplete, ...). The scanner records the rows (table llm_coverage) after every LLM run and snapshot save and recounts stale ones with the llm_coverage job; no model is called for it.

docs.title: Default rules of a new installation
docs.text:
Migration 0013_example_rules seeds two LLM object rules in mode auto with mark_fields (one call per object marks it and the fields the model names); each is skipped when a live rule already has its name:

rule category / severity / tags scope state db-tables-with-client-data pii / high / personal-data object_type_re: table enabled api-with-auth auth / critical / auth-data object_type_re: route|rpc|query|mutation disabled - enable it in the UI / API / MCP

db-tables-with-client-data marks database tables that store personal data of natural persons and their columns; api-with-auth marks API operations whose request or response carries authentication secrets (passwords, PIN / OTP codes, access / refresh / session tokens, API keys, client secrets, private keys, CVV; not logins, ids, roles or public keys). Their match verdicts score the objects at once but stay in the tiered workflow: they are part of the harness model's QA sample, their need_more_info verdicts are escalated, and a harness or human decision overrides them.

There is no env-managed LLM rule (LLM_PROMPT is gone): an LLM field rule without category made in the UI / REST / MCP is the built-in classifier.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: An object's tags are read at query time: the tags of the rules of its match hits plus the tags of manual labels. Rule tags are edited in the UI (also on the built-in rules). GET /objects?filter={"tag": "gdpr"} and MCP list_objects(tags=[...]) filter by them; the Landscape page shows where the data of a category / tag lives.

docs.title: Manual labels and inventory mode
docs.text: A project in scan mode inventory (PATCH /projects/{id} {"scan_mode": "inventory"}, MCP set_scan_mode) is parsed without categorisation. Objects and fields are labelled by hand: UI Objects page, REST POST /objects/{key}/labels / DELETE, POST /objects/labels (bulk), MCP label / unlabel / label_bulk. A label is a match hit of the built-in manual:labels rule (kind manual) with the reviewer set, so scans never overwrite it; it shows up in /hits like any decision. Labels work in rules mode too.

docs.title: External parser states
docs.text: Objects pushed with POST /ingest go through the keyword rules (and the LLM rules with llm: true) like parsed code: External parsers.

docs.title: Scanning and change detection
docs.text:
The scanner polls GitLab; there are no webhooks. Everything it does is a job of the Postgres queue (see Jobs and workers).

scheduler -> sync_projects (every PROJECTS_POLL_INTERVAL_S, a full sync first after start-up)
          -> sync_branches_mrs      per new / changed project
               -> scan_branch       main branch with a new commit            (GITLAB_SCAN_TYPES mains)
                    -> llm_score    after a successful main scan (LLM_API_URL set; not after a diff-based skip)
                         -> llm_verify   verify items for the harness model
               -> scan_mr           open MR with activity in the last day    (GITLAB_SCAN_TYPES mrs)
scheduler -> cleanup (every GC_INTERVAL_HOURS), llm_coverage (every LLM_COVERAGE_INTERVAL_S),
             llm_rollout (every LLM_ROLLOUT_TICK_S)

docs.title: Projects and branches
docs.text:
sync_projects lists the projects of every GITLAB_PROJECTS_PREFIX (matched on path segments: grp/ is the group, grp/proj that project only, grp/proj* a plain string prefix) and queues sync_branches_mrs for the projects whose GitLab activity (last_activity_at) is newer than what was processed, and for the ones not re-read for SYNC_UNCHANGED_EVERY_H (24 h: stale MRs are released and deleted branches noticed even without activity; the full sync after start-up follows the same rule, every project only with the setting at 0). That job reads the project, its open MRs (one page of 100), the default branch (the project's main) and the branches of the non-stale open MRs by name - not every branch of the repository, which cost a page of 20 per call - and the states of the MRs that left the open list in one batched call per 100 (iids[]); it tracks the MR source branches and queues the scans. The sync runs on its own worker pool (SYNC_WORKERS), so the harness verify items, external answers and rollouts of the control pool never wait behind it. Projects of a prefix removed from the configuration stay in the database until deleted.

Main branch: scan_branch clones the branch at its head commit into a temporary workspace of the job, runs the parsers of PARSERS (when SCAN_LANGS lists the project's language, or is all), applies the keyword rules of the project and saves the snapshot in one transaction: objects and fields (content-addressed, see Data model), the diff to the previous snapshot, keyword hits, scanned_commit, the deltas of MRs now merged. When LLM_API_URL is set an llm_score job follows with every enabled LLM rule. Dedup keys contain the commit, so a commit pushed while a scan runs is queued as a new job.

Merge requests: scan_mr makes sure the target's snapshot is current (scans the target main first if needed), scans the source branch and stores only the delta against the target - objects added, modified or removed by the MR (branch_objects.change) - then runs the LLM rules on the delta. MRs are scanned automatically only when they were updated in the last day; POST /mrs/{id}/scan / MCP scan_mr scans one at any time. Hits on MR objects are reviewed like any other (presence "Only in open MRs"); the MR itself is reached through GET /mrs, GET /mrs/{id} and MCP list_mrs / get_mr. Closed / merged MRs lose their tracked source branch and delta, stale open ones (MR_STALE_DAYS) likewise.

Hits are branch-agnostic: one hit per rule and subject, whatever branch the subject is in; a decision made on the MR version of an object holds for the main version.

docs.title: Re-parsing on demand
docs.text: POST /projects/parse (MCP parse_projects, UI Projects page "Parse"): {"project_ids": [1, 5], "parsers": ["protobuf"], "mains": true, "mrs": true, "llm": false, "force": false} clones and parses projects again, e.g. after a keyword rule edit. Without project_ids every project; with parsers only those run and only their objects are replaced (the other parsers' objects are kept). LLM rules are off by default. A keyword rule edit also makes the branches rescan once by itself (scan markers carry the rules' versions).

docs.title: Scan modes
docs.text: PATCH /projects/{id} {"scan_mode": "inventory"} (MCP set_scan_mode, UI Projects page): an inventory project is parsed without categorisation - no keyword or LLM rules - and labelled by hand (Rules: manual labels). The default mode is rules.

docs.title: Diff-based scan skip
docs.text:
Every new commit of a main branch used to mean a full clone and every parser, although most commits touch no file a parser reads. Before cloning, the scanner asks the GitLab compare API (polling, no webhooks) which files changed since the commit its snapshot reflects (gitlab_branches.scanned_commit) and checks them against the files each parser declares it reads (core Parser.file_patterns: *.proto; *.graphql / *.gql; *.js / *.jsx / *.ts / *.tsx / *.mjs / *.cjs; *.sql; *.go; *.java; *.py / *.pyi; *.yaml / *.yml / *.json; *.tf / *.tf.json; appsec_discovery.affected_parsers). When no changed file is read by a parser of the scan, the snapshot is moved to the new commit (scanned_commit, a scan marker and the LLM coverage rows; objects, hits and verdicts untouched, no LLM run) and the job ends in seconds with progress = {"phase": "skipped", "skipped": "no parser files changed", "changed_files": N}.

A full scan happens anyway (the clone phase records why in progress.full_scan_reason) when:

  • the snapshot is missing, or was made with another scan configuration (gitlab_branches.scan_fingerprint: core package version, parsers, keyword rules, scan mode; stored with every full scan, so an upgrade or a rule edit rescans every branch once);
  • the last full scan is older than SCAN_FULL_RESCAN_DAYS (default 7; 0 = never on time alone);
  • the scanned commit is not an ancestor of the new one (force push / rebase, GitLab merge base API);
  • the compare is truncated (compare_timeout, or SCAN_DIFF_MAX_FILES files or more, default 1000);
  • a changed file matches SCAN_ALWAYS_RESCAN_GLOBS (comma separated globs, default empty; a pattern with / matches the repository path, one without matches the file name); go.mod / package.json count while the SCAN_LANGS gate is on, because the language detection reads them;
  • the compare API fails for any reason (logged with the cause, credentials stripped; the shortcut never fails a job).

Merge requests (SCAN_DIFF_SKIP_MRS, default true): the stored delta is kept only when neither the source (since the scanned source commit) nor the target (since the target commit the delta was computed against, gitlab_branches.delta_target_commit) moved in parser files; the same fingerprint / age / ancestry rules apply to the source branch. A full MR scan takes the files the MR changes from the compare of the merge base (the same set as git diff --name-only <merge-base> HEAD, both paths of a rename) and clones the source shallow; the git diff in a history clone stays the fallback when that compare is truncated or fails. A main target behind its snapshot is moved the same way instead of being cloned and scanned for the MR.

Visibility: the Jobs page shows skipped: no parser files changed (N files) or full scan: <reason>; GET /scan_progress counts a skipped branch as scanned_current (its snapshot is at the head commit); GET /jobs/health (MCP job_health) adds skipped_24h per kind and scans (scan_branch / scan_mr: full vs skipped in the last 24 hours), shown on the Pipeline health page (Parse tile "24 h: X full, Y skipped scans", queue table "Done 1h / 24h (N skipped)"). No llm_score job follows a skipped scan.

Settings (scanner): SCAN_DIFF_SKIP=true (false restores the previous behaviour exactly: every commit cloned and parsed, MR sources cloned with history), SCAN_DIFF_SKIP_MRS=true, SCAN_FULL_RESCAN_DAYS=7, SCAN_DIFF_MAX_FILES=1000, SCAN_ALWAYS_RESCAN_GLOBS=. Migration 0029_diff_skip adds the branch columns; existing branches are fully scanned once at their next commit and skipped from then on. Core 1.1.0 adds Parser.file_patterns and appsec_discovery.affected_parsers / parser_file_patterns.

docs.title: Disk space of clones
docs.text:
Every scan job clones into its own directory under WORKSPACE_DIR and removes it when the job ends, success or not; a worker that died leaves its directory behind, and the supervisor removes it (at once, and all of them at start-up). Clones do not pile up: the disk holds at most the clones of the running scan jobs (MAX_WORKERS, an MR scan holds the source and the target). Main branches and MR targets are cloned with --depth 1; an MR source whose changed files the compare API could not give keeps its history as a partial clone (--filter=blob:none: all commits and trees, the file contents of the checkout only; GIT_PARTIAL_CLONE=false clones the full history).

Guards before a clone:

  • WORKSPACE_MIN_FREE_GB=5: no clone starts while the file system of the workspace has less free space. The job fails with not enough disk space for a clone: N GB free in the workspace and is retried with backoff; the cause is one row of "Needs attention" on the Pipeline health page. 0 disables the check. A clone that fills the disk anyway fails with no space left on device (transient) and its partial checkout is removed at once.
  • SCAN_MAX_REPO_MB=0: a repository GitLab reports larger (statistics.repository_size, the whole history, so a shallow clone is smaller) is not cloned: the job fails at once with repository too large: N MB (permanent). 0: no limit. Without Reporter access GitLab gives no statistics and the limit does not apply.

In the bundled compose the workspace is the volume scan_workspace mounted at /workspace (WORKSPACE_DIR). It is on the Docker disk, next to the Postgres volume: the free-space guard keeps clones from taking the last WORKSPACE_MIN_FREE_GB of it. To keep clones off the database disk entirely, set SCAN_WORKSPACE_VOLUME to a host directory on another disk (SCAN_WORKSPACE_VOLUME=/mnt/scans).

docs.title: Progress of parse scans
docs.text:
GET /scan_progress (MCP scan_progress; computed from the database, no GitLab calls) reports, for the tracked GitLab projects (source = gitlab; external POST /ingest projects are counted apart under external):

  • main: how many projects are synced (branches and MRs re-read for their latest activity; sync_queued / sync_running) and the state of each main branch, exactly one of scanned_current (snapshot at the head commit, a diff-based skip included), outdated (snapshot of an older commit), never_scanned, partial (a parser failed at the head commit, retried), failed (the last scan_branch job used up its attempts), skipped (the last scan job of the head commit saved nothing: SCAN_LANGS gate) and no_main; queued / running / retrying count the main branches with a scan_branch job pending / running / pending after a failed attempt; the same by scan mode (by_scan_mode: rules, inventory).
  • mrs: open MRs: scanned_current (delta at the MR's source commit), outdated, never_scanned, partial, failed, not_tracked (no tracked branches, or another open MR of the source branch owns the delta), queued, running.
  • queue: active jobs by kind; the last sync_projects job.
  • projects: the projects, problems first (?status=failed,partial or queued, running, active, attention, not_synced, any state; scan_mode, q, project_id=1,5, limit up to 500, offset; projects=false for totals only) with commit / scanned commit, last scan, job, last error and open MR counts.

The Pipeline health page shows it as "Parse" (bars, counts, projects that failed or wait), the Projects page as the "Parse" column. scan_branch jobs carry their phase in progress: waiting -> clone -> parse -> save (with objects, by_parser, failed_parsers) -> done | skipped | partial | failed.

docs.title: Tiered review: service model, harness model, human
docs.text:
LLM verdicts are made in three tiers. Every hit records who made its current decision in decided_tier:

tier who how service the service model - the LLM the scanner calls (LLM_API_URL, usually a cheap local model) categorises everything: every LLM rule run harness the harness model - a capable model in an agent harness (e.g. Claude Code) connected to the MCP server checks what the service model was unsure about and a sample of what it was sure about human a reviewer in the UI, REST or MCP decides what the harness model cannot, and anything else

Precedence: the service model never overwrites a harness or human decision, the harness model never a human one. A harness answer about a hit a human decided meanwhile, or whose service verdict changed, is refused as stale.

service LLM run  -->  verdicts, decided_tier 'service'
       |
       v  llm_verify job (control worker, after every service run of a branch; no model call)
verify items (llm_work_items.purpose = 'verify', one per hit):
   escalation  every service need_more_info verdict                      (LLM_VERIFY_ESCALATE, default on;
                                                                          LLM_ESCALATION_DAILY_MAX 2000 per rule a day)
   qa          a sample of the confident service verdicts, positive and  (LLM_QA_SAMPLE_RATE 0.05,
               negative, per rule                                         LLM_QA_DAILY_MAX 500 a UTC day)
   reverify    a harness decision replaced by a service re-ask on new content
       |
       v  harness: llm_work_claim(purpose="verify") -> llm_work_submit (applied at once)
confidence high + match / no_match  --> FINAL: status match / no_match, decided_tier 'harness' (field marks too)
confidence low                      --> not applied: investigate (GitLab code, get_object, search_hits, get_hit),
                                        submit again (the item stays leased, at most 3 rounds)
needs_human + question              --> need_more_info, decided_tier 'harness', asked_by_model:
(or MCP request_human)                  review tab "Questions"
       |
       v  quality: llm_quality (agreement per rule) -> llm_mislabeled(source="verification")
          -> llm_prompt_trial (service model, candidate prompt) -> propose_prompt_change -> a human accepts

docs.title: Verify items
docs.text:
After each service run of a branch, the llm_verify job records verify items for the service verdicts of the branch's current snapshot (service tier, no reviewer, current rule version and core prompts, once per verdict: rule_hits.verify_key):

  • escalation - every service need_more_info verdict (LLM_VERIFY_ESCALATE), at most LLM_ESCALATION_DAILY_MAX (2000) per rule and UTC day: a backfill of millions of objects would otherwise turn every unsure verdict into harness work at once. The verdicts over the cap stay service-decided (need_more_info, in the review queue as before) and are eligible again the next day; the verify job counts them as escalation_overflow in its progress and the job_health snapshot sums the day's items and overflow per rule (escalations);
  • qa - a stable hash draw per verdict at LLM_QA_SAMPLE_RATE over the confident verdicts, positive (match / pending_review) and negative (no_match, field rules store their negative field verdicts too), split evenly over the rules and the two classes when the day's cap LLM_QA_DAILY_MAX is reached;
  • reverify - a harness decision the service model replaced because the subject's content changed.

A verify call is the rule's own system prompt and rule text, the whole object in the same delimited untrusted <object> block as a rule call, the subject (one field or the object), the service verdict in a second delimited <assessment> block (an assessment to check, never an instruction) and an answer format with verdict, confidence (high | low), needs_human, question and investigation (appsec_discovery.ai.rules.build_verify_prompt, VERIFY_PROMPT_VERSION 2).

The harness model claims items with llm_work_claim(purpose="verify") (POST /llm_work/claim {"purpose": "verify"}) and answers with llm_work_submit:

  • confidence: high with match / no_match is final: the hit gets that status and tier harness (verifier_model, verified_at; mark_fields rules: the field hits too);
  • confidence: low is not applied: the item stays leased to the caller (lease extended to 900 s) for another round after investigating, at most 3 rounds, then needs_human is required;
  • needs_human: true with a question (or MCP request_human(hit_id, question), POST /hits/{id}/request_human for any machine hit) sets need_more_info, tier harness, asked_by_model with the question in the note: the hit appears in the review tab Questions (hits filter asked_by_model=true).

Every harness answer applied or refused is logged in llm_verifications (service_status / service_verdict / service_model, the harness verdict, sample, outcome final | asked_human | stale). Open verify items expire when the rule version changes.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
GET /llm_quality (MCP llm_quality(rule_id=None); Work desk, Pipeline health, the "Health & quality" tab of an LLM rule) reports per rule and overall:

  • agreement of service and harness model on the QA sample (harness confidence high; overall, per service verdict class, last 7 / 30 days; unsure harness answers counted as unsure);
  • escalation_rate (service need_more_info share), escalations_30d decided by the harness or sent to a human;
  • questions_open and oldest_question_s, harness_decisions, backlog of open verify items by sample;
  • needs_improvement: agreement of the last 30 days below LLM_QA_AGREEMENT_MIN (0.9) with at least 30 samples.

GET /llm_work/stats (MCP llm_work_stats; the Harness work page) sums up the harness work: items by purpose and status, open verify items by sample, leases held by owner, answers of the last 24 hours by owner.

docs.title: Improving a prompt: trials and proposals
docs.text:
1. llm_mislabeled(rule_id, source="human" | "verification") (GET /llm_rules/{id}/mislabeled): the subjects a human or the harness model decided differently from the service model (rule_hits.machine_status).
  2. llm_prompt_trial(rule_id, prompt, subjects=[...] | from_mislabeled=true, include_controls=20, rerun_current=true) (POST /llm_rules/{id}/trials, UI "Try this prompt"): an llm_trial job runs the candidate system prompt with the service model on those subjects plus random controls whose verdict a human or the harness confirmed, and with rerun_current the current prompt on the same objects (a fair A/B). A trial writes no hits, coverage or rule change. Limits: prompt <= 20000 characters, LLM_TRIAL_MAX_SUBJECTS (200, controls included), LLM_TRIAL_DAILY_CALLS (2000 calls of all trials a UTC day; 429 beyond).
  3. llm_prompt_trial_result(trial_id) (GET /prompt_trials/{id}): per subject expected / current / re-run / new verdict; metrics: fixed, still wrong, newly wrong, control regressions, accuracy before -> after, calls, failures. llm_prompt_trials(rule_id) lists a rule's trials.
  4. propose_prompt_change(rule_id, prompt, trial_id, rationale) (POST /llm_rules/{id}/proposals) needs a finished trial of exactly that text (sha256) and changes nothing. prompt_proposals(rule_id, status) lists proposals.
  5. Only a human accepts: the Proposals tab of the LLM rule page (listed on the Work desk: diff, trial metrics and the re-ask cost, GET /prompt_proposals/{id}/reask) or POST /prompt_proposals/{id}/accept | reject. Accepting makes a candidate version of the rule ("Accept as candidate only") or activates it and starts its rollout ("Accept and roll out", activate: true); see LLM rule lifecycle. There is no MCP tool to accept a proposal or activate a version.

Candidate prompts from agents are stored and shown as data (a diff against the current prompt); the scanner sends them only as the rule's system prompt, the object stays in the delimited untrusted block.

docs.title: Human review
docs.text:
The Review page (Datasec role) is the triage view: tabs Questions (the harness model asked a human), Pending (pending_review), Model unsure (need_more_info not asked by the model), Verified by harness (match / no_match with tier harness), All; an evidence panel (object, fields with comments and samples, the model's reason and verifier, presence in branches / MRs, other hits on the object); keyboard shortcuts j / k move, c / r / i confirm / reject / request info, u reopen, x select for the bulk actions, o open the hit page, ? help. The same decisions: REST POST /hits/{id}/review (confirm | reject | request_info | reopen, with category, severity, note), POST /hits/review_bulk, MCP confirm / reject / request_info / reopen / update_category / review_hits_bulk (up to 50, note required, dry_run first). Decisions record the reviewer and decided_via (rest | mcp) and make the hit's tier human.

Deciding by filter (tens of thousands of open hits): GET /hits/clusters?by=schema | field_pattern | object_name | rule_group (MCP hits_clusters) groups the open hits into clusters - the same table schema copied into many services, one field name everywhere, one object name, one rule in one GitLab group - with counts, projects, the share in main, the new ones of the last 7 days, the questions inside (answer those first) and sample ids to look at. POST /hits/decide (MCP decide_hits) applies one action to every hit of a filter (cluster, rule_id, group, status, ... as GET /hits): the dry run (default) says how many hits would change and what is kept - human decisions are never overwritten (unless a human asks for it with include_human), the harness model's questions are skipped, the transitions above apply - and the apply needs expected_total equal to that figure (409 when the set changed meanwhile). Every apply is a review_batches row with the previous state of each hit; POST /hits/decide/{batch_id}/undo restores the hits nobody decided again since; the verdict history of each hit carries batch_id. GET /hits/aggregate gives the counts behind the tabs and tiles (by queue, rule, category, project, group, ...) in one call.

docs.title: UI
docs.text: http://<host>/, login with UI_ADMIN_EMAIL and the password of UI_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH (one user; decisions are recorded under it). The UI calls the REST API under /api.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
The app bar has a switch View as: Admin | Datasec. The role orders the menu and picks the home page; it is remembered per browser (the stored choice of the old name "Engineer" is read as Datasec) and every page stays reachable in both roles (the other role's pages sit in a collapsed section at the end of the menu).

role who home menu Admin keeps the pipeline going: scans, LLM runs, harness work Pipeline health Pipeline: Pipeline health, Jobs, Groups, Projects, Ingest batches, Harness work; Settings: Service tokens; collapsed: Review & rules Datasec writes rules, reviews hits, improves prompts Work desk Work: Work desk, Review; Rules: LLM rules, Keyword rules; Landscape: Landscape, Objects, Groups, Projects; Harness: Harness work; collapsed: Pipeline & settings

docs.title: Scope: a GitLab group
docs.text: The app bar has Scope: [group] (autocomplete over GET /groups): a prefix of the projects' full_path (grp/payments means grp/payments/ledger-svc and everything below, not grp/payments-old). It is kept in the URL (?scope=grp/payments, so a link carries it; a link with another scope wins over the remembered one) and per browser. Every hits / objects / projects list and every count, cluster and decision of the Review page, the Work desk, the Pipeline "Human" tile, the Landscape "By group" panel and the Group view sends it as group=; the page titles name it ("Review · grp/payments"). Jobs have no group filter (the project filter instead).

docs.title: At scale
docs.text:
• Totals are estimates above 10 000 rows: the Review, Objects and Projects lists say "about N rows (estimate)" with an exact count action (one count(*) on click, never per page; X-Total-Estimate).
  • Keyset paging: paging forward continues from the previous page's cursor (X-Next-Cursor / after=), so a deep page costs one index probe; a jump to a far page without a cursor falls back to the offset.
  • One queue definition (choices.js QUEUES): the Review tabs, the Review menu badge, the Work desk tiles, the Pipeline "Human" tile and the Group view count the same sets (questions / pending / model unsure: live hits without the field marks of object rules) from one GET /hits/aggregate?by=queue each, served from the scanner's statistics snapshot. Counts reload two seconds after a decision, not on every page of the list.
  • Snapshots: the Pipeline health, Work desk and the autocompletes read the statistics snapshots (ETag, 304) and say "updated N s ago" (or "live" when the snapshot was stale and the API computed). Polling waits for the previous answer, runs four times slower in a hidden tab and backs off after errors.
  • No silent truncation: wherever the API caps a list or an aggregate the page says "N of M shown" / "top N" / "first 200 of N" (Landscape top 200 projects, Parse / Run rules next actions, Retry of the first 50 ids, cluster pages, aggregate rows, rule runs).
  • Server-side autocompletes: rules (GET /rules?q=, both kinds), categories (GET /categories), object types (GET /object_types), groups (GET /groups?q=) instead of loading 500 rules or the whole overview per dropdown.

docs.text:
page what it shows Pipeline health (/pipeline) is the pipeline GitLab sync -> Parse -> Service model -> Harness model -> Human keeping up: a tile per stage with the backlog, the oldest waiting age and the hourly rate (Parse: full vs skipped scans in 24 h; Harness: today's escalations against the daily cap LLM_ESCALATION_DAILY_MAX and the overflow kept service-decided; Human: questions, pending, unsure from the queues aggregate); Job queue (per kind: waiting / running / failed, done 1h / 24h with skipped counts, oldest waiting coloured against the kind's typical wait, typical run / wait, throughput and ETA; idle kinds collapsed), Workers with the pools and limits (scan / sync / control / llm workers, LLM concurrency, rate limit tokens left), Failures (24 h) grouped by cause, Parse details, LLM coverage, Rule runs, Rollouts. Next actions say their reach ("Parse first 200 of 1 480 behind"). Sources: the snapshots /jobs/health, /scan_progress, /llm_progress, /llm_quality (ETag, "updated N s ago"), /llm_work/stats, /llm_runs, /llm_rollouts, /jobs/errors, /hits/aggregate Work desk (/workdesk) what waits for me: Questions (from the harness model), Clusters to decide, Pending review, Model unsure (the same numbers as the Review tabs), open Proposals, Rules (health); the top 10 clusters (same schema across services) with "Decide"; Open hits by rule (questions / pending / unsure per rule, from the aggregate); New in 24 h; Rule health with a search box and "only rules that need attention"; Coverage of the LLM rules Review (/hits) tabs Questions / To decide / Pending / Model unsure / Verified by harness / All, counted by one GET /hits/aggregate; two views: Clusters (default for the open queues): the open hits grouped by Same schema, Same field, Same object name or Rule x group x type (GET /hits/clusters) with open count, projects, groups, in-main share, new in 7 days, questions inside, severity; a row opens the cluster panel (5 sample hits with the evidence panel, keys j / k, c / r / i decide the cluster, l opens it as a list, Esc); Decide opens the decision dialog: a note (required), the dry run (POST /hits/decide: how many change, what is kept - human and harness decisions, the model's questions, status transitions - by project, a sample), Apply to N sends the dry run's figure as expected_total (the server refuses when the set changed and the dry run runs again), then a toast "Batch #id ... Undo" for a minute and the "Recent decisions by filter" section (GET /review_batches) with Undo per batch. List (the Questions tab, "Verified by harness", a cluster opened as a list, or the toggle): the triage view - the list with an evidence panel (object, fields with comments and samples, the model's reason and verifier, presence in branches / MRs, other hits, history with batch ids), shortcuts j / k, c / r / i / u, x, o, ?, bulk decisions on selected hits (at most 50) and Decide all on everything the current filter matches (server side, dry run, undo). A row opens the project page (/projects/:id/show, GET /projects/{id}): tiles Parse, LLM rules, Open hits, Open MRs (objects only in open MRs - MRs are markers, not a page), Objects (main); Hits by rule (match / no match / open / questions, every figure a link into Review), Objects by type, the last 20 jobs with a link to the Jobs page filtered to the project; Review hits / Objects / Jobs / Parse actions. Every project link in the UI (hits, objects, jobs, Landscape, Parse details, LLM coverage) opens this page Jobs (/jobs) the queue with tabs Active / Failed 24 h / All; filters error text, kind, project, status; the subject's project links to the project page; a job page with progress, the subject, the real failure cause, Retry (failed) and Cancel (pending); run times from started_at Harness work (/harness) the harnesses connected over MCP (answers in the last hour, leases, "gone?" when a claimed item has had no answer for an hour), checks queued for the harness model, external runs with Take over / Release to service, pending service runs, refused answers, MCP snippets to copy (the connect snippet takes a per-harness token with scope mcp) Ingest batches (/ingest) the states pushed by external collectors (POST /ingest), their status and jobs Service tokens (/tokens) admin only: tokens for collectors (scope ingest on project prefixes under external/) and for harnesses / agents (scope mcp: the client acts as token:<name> on REST and MCP, with its own rate limit, revocable on its own); created once, shown once with the MCP connect command for mcp tokens, revoked by delete; "Last used" links to the token's batches or decisions

There is no merge requests page: an MR is a marker on a hit or an object (Only in open MR = the code is not in a main branch yet), a row "Only in open MRs" on the project page and in Landscape, and the filter presence "Only in open MRs" in Objects and Review. MR data is reached through GET /mrs, GET /mrs/{id}, POST /mrs/{id}/scan and the MCP tools list_mrs / get_mr / scan_mr. There are no alerts: the service never posts to GitLab or messengers.

The words of the UI (statuses, tiers, modes, actions, queues, presence) are one glossary (discovery_ui/src/choices.js): hit statuses Pending review / Needs more info / Match / No match; decided by Service model / Harness model / Human; actions Mark as match / Mark as no match / Ask for more info / Reopen; queues Questions / Pending / Model unsure; presence In main / Only in open MR / Gone.
